Front: What two methods must a custom nn.Module define, and what does each do?
Back: __init__ (call super().__init__(), instantiate/register submodules so PyTorch tracks their parameters) and forward (defines the forward computation). Call model(x) not .forward(); backward is auto-derived.

Front: What is the core structural idea of a Siamese network?
Back: Twin subnetworks that SHARE weights. Both inputs pass through the same backbone into a common embedding space, then you compare by distance/similarity. Weight sharing is what keeps both embeddings in the same space.

Front: Why use similarity learning (Siamese) instead of a classifier for face/signature verification?
Back: Open-set, few-shot: many identities, few samples each, new ones constantly. A classifier needs fixed classes + retraining to add one. Siamese learns a general similarity metric, so enrolling someone new is just storing a reference embedding; generalizes to unseen identities.

Inputs: anchor, positive, negative. Objective (relative): d(anchor,negative) > d(anchor,positive) + margin. Loss = max(0, d(a,p) - d(a,n) + margin). Pull positive close, push negative far, only up to the margin. Positive is never pushed away.

Front: What problem do ResNet skip connections solve, and how?
Back: Vanishing gradients and the degradation problem (deep plain nets get worse on training error). Block computes F(x) + x; the +x path has derivative 1 so gradient flows back unchanged (gradient highway). Also lets a block learn identity by driving F(x) -> 0.

Front: Key difference between ResNet and DenseNet connections?
Back: ResNet ADDS: F(x) + x, element-wise sum, channels constant. DenseNet CONCATENATES: each layer receives the stacked feature maps of all preceding layers; channels grow by the growth rate k. Concatenation gives feature reuse and fewer params than expected.

Front: What do DenseNet transition layers do?
Back: Sit between dense blocks and keep growth in check: 1x1 conv to compress channels (compression factor ~0.5) + 2x2 average pooling to downsample spatially. Without them channels and feature-map size explode.

Front: How do you write a Siamese forward for a pair, and what must you NOT do?
Back: Call the SAME backbone on each input: e1 = self.backbone(x1); e2 = self.backbone(x2); return e1, e2. Do NOT create two separate backbones - that breaks weight sharing and the embeddings no longer share a space.

Front: At inference, how does an embedding model decide same vs different?
Back: Embed both inputs with the shared backbone, compute distance (Euclidean) or cosine similarity, compare to a THRESHOLD (distance below = same; for cosine, above = same). The threshold is chosen once on a validation set (ROC trade-off of false accept vs reject), fixed at inference.

Front: How do you build visual search with a trained embedding network?
Back: Train the embedding net; precompute + store embeddings for the whole database offline; at query time embed the query and return top-K nearest by distance. Use an approximate NN index (e.g. FAISS) at scale. Negatives matter only in training; retrieval is pure nearest-neighbor.
